summary: Daniel Veidlinger is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD at the University of Chicago under Steven Collins, Nalini Devdas, and Samli Mulkæo. He was a research associate at Chiang Mai University (1999) and held a post at California State University, Chico.

Daniel W. Kent is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Virginia, where he was an instructor in 2010, the same year he also served as an instructor at Mary Baldwin University.

Daniela Berti is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD in Research Methodology in Ethno-Anthropology from the University of Siena. In 2004, she held a fellowship at Milieux, Cultures et Sociétés en Himalaya.

Daniela Bevilacqua specializes in Indology and religious studies. She earned PhDs from the University of Rome and Paris Nanterre University, and served as a post-doctoral research fellow at SOAS University of London in 2020.
Daniele Cuneo, who taught Arinde L. Jonker, held posts attested in 2018 at the University of Paris and the Sorbonne.
Danielle Feller is an Indologist who completed her PhD in 2001 at the University of Lausanne under doctoral supervisor Johannes Bronkhorst, having also studied under Ganesh U. Thite.

Daoquan Yu was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied at Cheeloo University (~1920–1924) and under Jacques Bacot (~1937–1938). He served as a professor at Minzu University of China from circa 1953 to 1992.

Dasharatha Sharma was an Indologist and historian educated at the University of Delhi. He served as Reader at Delhi (~1960–1969), Professor and Dean at Jai Narain Vyas University (1966), and Director of the Rajasthan Oriental Research Institute (~1969–1974).

Historian and Indologist Daud Ali studied at William & Mary and the University of Chicago, completing his PhD under Ronald Inden in 1996. He taught history at SOAS (~1995–2009) before becoming associate professor of South Asian history at the University of Pennsylvania in 2009.
David A. Dilworth works in philosophy and Japanology. He studied under Valdo H. Viglielmo and Masao Abe, and held an academic post at Stony Brook University around 1971.

David A. Hall is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology who studied under Shoshin Ichishima and earned his doctorate from UC Berkeley in 1990. He was a visiting scholar at Taisho University (1977) and later chaired STEM at Montgomery College.
David Azzopardi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from SOAS University of London, where he studied under Kate Crosby.

David B. Gray is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religion who earned his Ph.D. at Columbia under Robert A. F. Thurman and Ryuichi Abe. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Rice and an assistant professor at Santa Clara University.

David Brainerd Spooner was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Stanford University (~1895–1899). He served in the Archaeological Survey of India from circa 1906 until 1925 as Directeur p. i.

David Brick is an Indologist who studied under Patrick Olivelle. He served on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies in 2012 and held a professorship at Yale University attested between 2012 and 2018.

David Brown was an Indology and religious studies figure who studied at Magdalene College under Joseph Milner. He founded the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society and served as Provost of Fort William College from circa 1800 to 1807.

David Bubna-Litic earned a PhD from Western Sydney University. In 2000, he worked in Buddhist studies and served as a Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney.

David Burton, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, completed his doctoral thesis at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). He held posts as a Junior Research Fellow at Keble College (2001) and Senior Lecturer at Canterbury Christ Church University (2010).

David Drewes is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Virginia under Karen Christina Lang. He has held teaching posts at Virginia, Indiana University (2006), and the University of Manitoba (2008–2010).

David E. Cooper is a philosopher who studied at St Edmund Hall. He served as a Lecturer at Oxford (1967), Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008), and Distinguished International Visiting Professor at Peking University (2022).
